preamble: Rounding of the close-mid back unrounded vowel [ɤ] to [o]. Pittayaporn (2009) reconstructs Proto-Tai with a mid back unrounded vowel *ɤ beside *o. In closed syllables short *ɤ is reflected as /o/ in all Southwestern Tai varieties, including Siamese (Thai), Lao, Lue, Black Tai and White Tai, and the same rounding took place in a number of Central and Northern Tai varieties such as Shangsi, Yongnan, Laibin and Yishan. Lungchow keeps /ɤ/ except before labial codas, where it became /u/, and Yay and most other Northern Tai dialects lowered it to /a/: Proto-Tai *mɤcᴰ 'ant' is Siamese mot, Lungchow mɤt and Yay mat. In open syllables, where only long *ɤː occurred, all Northern Tai dialects rounded the vowel and merged it with *oː, as in Yay θo 'straight' and so 'name', whereas Siamese and Lungchow raised it to ɯː. Li (1977) reconstructs *oC for the closed-syllable set, which would leave Southwestern Tai unchanged; Pittayaporn's *ɤ follows Sarawit (1973) and Wang (1966).

examples.note: Wiktionary gives Proto-Southwestern Tai *motᴰˢ⁴: the rounding predates the break-up of Southwestern Tai. Lungchow mɤt keeps the unrounded vowel; Yay mat lowered it.
Lungchow kup was raised before the labial coda; Yay has kap.

In open syllables Pittayaporn (2009) has *ɤː rounded and merged with *oː in all Northern Tai dialects and in Central Tai Yongnan, Long'an, Fusui, Shangsi and Chongzuo. Siamese has ชื่อ cʰɯː and Lungchow cɯː instead.

sources: Pittayaporn, P. (2009). The Phonology of Proto-Tai. PhD dissertation, Cornell University. https://hdl.handle.net/1813/13855
